title: Before good fathers we speak freely
source_text: Οἱ δὲ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ παραπλήσιοι τοῖς ἐν ταῖς οἰκίαις ἐριουργοῖς ὅμοιοι δὲ καὶ τοῖς σκυτοτόμοις καὶ κναφεῦσι καὶ ἀπαιδευτοτάτοις ἀγροίκοις παρόντος μὲν πατρὸς καὶ διδασκάλων οὐδέν φησι λέγειν ἐθελήσουσιν οὐδὲ δυνήσονται τοῖς παισὶν ἑρμηνεύειν ἀγαθόν. καὶ πρὸς τοῦτο δ᾿ ἐροῦμεν· ποίου φῂς. ὦ οὗτος, πατρὸς καὶ ποίου διδασκάλου; εἰ μὲν τοῦ ἀρετὴν ἀποδεχομένου καὶ κακίαν ἀποστρεφομένου καὶ ἀσπαζομένου τὰ κρείττονα, ἄκουε ὅτι καὶ μάλα θαῤῥοῦντες ὡς εὐδοκιμοῦντες παρὰ τῷ τοιούτῳ κριτῇ ἐροῦμεν τοῖς παισὶ τὰ ἡμέτερα. εἰ δ᾿ ἐνώπιον πατρὸς διαβεβοημένου πρὸς ἀρετὴν καὶ καλοκἀγαθίαν σιωπῶμεν καὶ τῶν τὰ ἐναντία τῷ ὑγιεῖ λόγῳ διδασκόντων, τοῦτο μηδ᾿ ἡμῖν ἐγκάλει, οὐ γὰρ εὐλόγως ἐγκαλεῖς, καὶ σὺ γοῦν τὰ φιλοσοφίας ὄργια τοῖς νέοις καὶ υἱοῖς, πατέρων ἀργὸν πρᾶγμα καὶ ἀνωφελὲς νομιζόντων φιλοσοφίαν, παραδιδοὺς τοῖς παισὶν οὐκ ἐπὶ τῶν φαύλων πατέρων ἐρεῖς· ἀλλὰ βουλόμενος χωρίζεσθαι τοὺς προτραπέντας ἐπὶ φιλοσοφίαν υἱοὺς τῶν μοχθηρῶν πατέρων ἐπιτηρήσεις καιροὺς, ἵνα καθίκωνται οἱ φιλοσοφίας λόγοι τῶν νέων, καὶ περὶ τῶν διδασκάλων δὲ τὰ αὐτὰ φήσομεν, εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἀποτρέπομεν διδασκάλων διδασκόντων τὰ ἄσεμνα τῆς κωμῳδίας καὶ τοὺς ἀκολάστους τῶν ἰάμβων καὶ ὅσα ἄλλα, ἃ μήτε τὸν λέγοντα ἐπιστρέφει μήτε τοὺς ἀκούοντας ὠφελεῖ, καὶ μὴ εἰδότας φιλοσόφως ἀκούειν ποιημάτων καὶ ἐπιλέγειν ἑκάστοις τὰ συντείνοντα εἰς ὠφέλειαν τῶν νέων, τοῦτο ποιοῦντες οὐκ αἰσχυνόμεθα ὁμολογεῖν τὸ πραττόμενον· εἰ δὲ παραστήσεις μοι διδασκάλους πρὸς φιλοσοφίαν προπαιδεύοντας καὶ ἐν φιλοσοφίᾳ γυμνάζοντας, οὐκ ἀποτρέψω μὲν ἀπὸ τούτων τοὺς νέους πειράσομαι δὲ προγυμνασαμένους αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐν ἐγκυκλίοις μαθήμασι καὶ τοῖς φιλοσοφουμένοις ἀναβιβάσαι ἐπὶ τὸ σεμνὸν καὶ ὑψηλὸν τῆς λεληθυίας τοὺς πολλοὺς Χριστιανῶν μεγαλοφωνίας, περὶ τῶν μεγίστων καὶ ἀναγκαιοτάτων διαλαμβανόντων καὶ ἀποδεικνύντων καὶ παριστάντων αὐτὰ πεφιλοσοφῆσθαι παρὰ τοῖς τοῦ θεοῦ προφήταις καὶ τοῖς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀποστόλοις.
pass_a_gloss: Those in Celsus, resembling (παραπλήσιος) the wool-workers in houses and like (ὅμοιος) the cobblers and fullers and most uneducated rustics, with father and teachers present (πάρειμι), he says, will not wish to say anything nor be able to explain (ἑρμηνεύω) good to the children. To this we shall say: of what sort (ποῖος) do you say, you there (ὦ οὗτος), of father and of what teacher? If of one accepting (ἀποδέχομαι) virtue (ἀρετή) and turning from (ἀποστρέφομαι) vice (κακία) and embracing (ἀσπάζομαι) the better, hear that very confidently (μάλα θαρρέω), as being well regarded (εὐδοκιμέω) before such a judge (κριτής), we shall say our things to the children. But if before (ἐνώπιον) a father notorious (διαβοάομαι, pf. pass.) against (πρός) virtue and nobility (καλοκἀγαθία), and those teaching things contrary to sound reason (ὑγιὴς λόγος), we keep silent (σιωπάω), do not accuse (ἐγκαλέω) us of this, for you do not accuse reasonably (εὐλόγως). You at any rate (γοῦν), handing on (παραδίδωμι) the rites (ὄργια) of philosophy to the young and sons, [their] fathers thinking (νομίζω) philosophy an idle (ἀργός) and useless (ἀνωφελής) thing, will not speak to the boys before the base (φαῦλος) fathers; but wishing to separate (χωρίζω) the sons urged on (προτρέπω) to philosophy from the wicked (μοχθηρός) fathers you will watch for (ἐπιτηρέω) occasions (καιρός), so that the words of philosophy may reach (καθικνέομαι) the young. And about the teachers we shall say the same. For if we turn away (ἀποτρέπω) [the young] from teachers teaching the indecencies (τὰ ἄσεμνα) of comedy (κωμῳδία) and the licentious of the iambics (ἴαμβος) and whatever else neither turns/converts (ἐπιστρέφω) the speaker nor benefits (ὠφελέω) the hearers, and [the young] not knowing how to hear poems (ποίημα) philosophically (φιλοσόφως) and to select (ἐπιλέγω) from each the things tending (συντείνω) to the benefit (ὠφέλεια) of the young, doing this we are not ashamed (αἰσχύνομαι) to confess (ὁμολογέω) what is done. But if you present to me teachers giving preliminary education (προπαιδεύω) for philosophy and exercising (γυμνάζω) in philosophy, I shall not turn the young away from these, but I shall try, them having been pre-trained (προγυμνάζω) as in the general lessons (ἐγκύκλια μαθήματα) and philosophical studies (τὰ φιλοσοφούμενα), to lead up (ἀναβιβάζω) to the majestic (σεμνός) and lofty (ὑψηλός) of the grandeur of speech (μεγαλοφωνία) of Christians that has escaped the notice (λανθάνω) of the many, who treat (διαλαμβάνω) the greatest and most necessary things, and demonstrate (ἀποδείκνυμι) and present that these were philosophised (φιλοσοφέω, pf. pass.) by the prophets of God and the apostles of Jesus.
pass_b_english: But the people Celsus describes, who resemble the wool-workers in houses and are like the cobblers and fullers and the most uneducated rustics, “while the father and teachers are present,” he says, “will be neither willing to say anything nor able to explain anything good to the children.” To this too we shall reply: What sort of father do you mean, sir, and what sort of teacher? If one who welcomes virtue, turns away from vice and embraces what is better, then hear this: we shall speak our teaching to the children with great confidence, as men who stand well with such a judge. But if, in front of a father notorious for his opposition to virtue and nobility of character, and in front of those who teach things contrary to sound reason, we keep silent, do not blame us for this either, for you have no good reason to blame us.

You yourself, at any rate, when you hand on the sacred rites of philosophy to young men and sons whose fathers consider philosophy an idle and useless thing, will not speak to the boys in front of their worthless fathers; rather, wishing to separate from their wicked fathers the sons who have been drawn toward philosophy, you will watch for opportunities so that the words of philosophy may reach the young.

We shall say the same about the teachers as well. If we turn the young away from teachers who teach the indecencies of comedy, and licentious iambic verse, and whatever else neither reforms the speaker nor benefits hearers who do not know how to listen to poems as philosophers do and to pick out from each what tends to the benefit of the young, then in doing this we are not ashamed to admit what we do. But if you show me teachers who train the young beforehand for philosophy and exercise them in philosophy, I shall not turn the young away from them. Rather, once they have been trained beforehand, as it were, in the general course of studies and in philosophical reasoning, I shall try to lead them up to the majestic and lofty eloquence of Christians, hidden from the many, who discuss the greatest and most necessary matters, and who demonstrate and show that these were treated philosophically by the prophets of God and the apostles of Jesus.

choices.choice: Only the words Origen gives as Celsus’s (with φησί) are in double quotation marks; they repeat 3.55. διαβεβοημένου πρὸς ἀρετήν: literally ‘notorious in relation to virtue’; the contrast with the good father in the previous clause requires the hostile sense, rendered ‘notorious for his opposition to virtue’. τῷ ὑγιεῖ λόγῳ rendered ‘sound reason’ (not cited as Scripture). τὰ φιλοσοφίας ὄργια: Origen turns Celsus’s mystery language back on him; ‘sacred rites of philosophy’. ἃ μήτε τὸν λέγοντα ἐπιστρέφει: ἐπιστρέφω, ‘turn round, convert’; rendered ‘reforms’. καὶ μὴ εἰδότας … is accusative plural and agrees with τοὺς ἀκούοντας just before it (note the echo ἀκούοντας … ἀκούειν), so it describes the hearers who gain nothing, not the teachers (genitive); the English attaches it there and keeps τῶν νέων as ‘the young’. Origen moves from ‘we’ to ‘I’ in the last sentences; kept. τῆς λεληθυίας τοὺς πολλοὺς Χριστιανῶν μεγαλοφωνίας: ‘the eloquence of Christians, hidden from the many’; διαλαμβανόντων etc. agree with Χριστιανῶν. No Scripture quoted.
‘the people in Celsus’ (calque of οἱ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ) to ‘the people Celsus describes’
ὡς εὐδοκιμοῦντες: ‘sure of approval’ (added certainty) to ‘who stand well with such a judge’
οὐ γὰρ εὐλόγως ἐγκαλεῖς: present indicative, ‘you would have’ to ‘you have no good reason’
καὶ μὴ εἰδότας: re-attached to τοὺς ἀκούοντας (acc. pl., echo ἀκούειν); removed added ‘not yet’; ‘their benefit’ to ‘the benefit of the young’ (τῶν νέων); translator note updated
